preprocessing.reason: profile.json shows dense data (0.01% zeros) with values in [0, 255], and DATA_DESCRIPTION.md says these are raw 8-bit RGB pixel intensities from 28x28x3 H&E patches. That is a fixed, natural bound shared by every feature, so rescaling to [0, 1] puts all 2,352 pixels on the same footing without changing their relative contrast. Judgment call: standardize was the alternative, but it would give low-variance pixels (e.g. uniformly bright background regions) the same weight as informative ones, which the shared 0-255 scale already avoids. No count normalization or log1p: these are intensities, not counts. No select_top_variance: n_features (2,352) is far below n_samples (89,996), so dimensionality is not a problem that justifies discarding pixels.

methods.name: pca
methods.reason: Required linear baseline. n_components = min(50, floor(89996/2), 2352) = 50. Neighboring pixels and the three color channels of the same pixel are strongly correlated in natural images, so a few dozen components should capture most variance; the sidecar reports exactly how much and how many a 90% target would need. PCA is cheap at 89,996 samples.

methods.name: sparse_pca
methods.reason: Required PCA variant. n_samples = 89,996 is far above the ~5,000 threshold, so Kernel PCA (a 89,996 x 89,996 kernel matrix) is not feasible without subsampling; Sparse PCA runs on the full data. Its sparse loadings also suit image data, since each component uses a limited set of pixels/channels, which is easier to interpret than dense PCA loadings. Judgment call: n_components = 20 rather than PCA's 50, because method-selection/SKILL.md measured about 23 minutes for 50 components on this exact data shape and advises keeping it modest; 20 still spans the leading structure. Alternative was subsampling to ~5,000 and running Kernel PCA, rejected because it would analyse only about 6% of the images.

methods.name: umap
methods.reason: Visualization only. n_samples = 89,996 is above 20,000, so n_neighbors is raised to 30 to keep a broader local neighborhood in a dataset this large; min_dist = 0.1 is UMAP's default. The 9 tissue labels are used only to color it and for the label-silhouette sanity check. Never used for any computation.

methods.name: tsne
methods.reason: Second visualization layout, included for a specific reason: CLAUDE.md requires a second setting before trusting a structural claim from a manifold method, and only one UMAP artifact per method name is supported, so t-SNE (a different objective on the same preprocessed data) is the cross-check. A class-separation pattern is only described in the report if both UMAP and t-SNE show it. Perplexity 30 (sklearn default) is tiny relative to 89,996 samples; judgment call, since larger perplexity would emphasise more global structure but raises run time substantially at this size. Expected to be slow at ~90k points; still run on the full data rather than a subsample to keep one shared input across methods. Visualization only.
